metadata.note: The Santa Cruz Railroad, chartered 1873 by local Santa Cruz business interests (including F.A. Hihn) to end the town's rail isolation, built a narrow-gauge line east along the coast through Capitola and Aptos to Pajaro, where it connected with the Southern Pacific's Coast Line main line (Watsonville Junction). Geometry traced from OpenStreetMap active-rail data (way name=Santa Cruz Branch, the modern operating name for this same physical corridor), Dijkstra-traced with graph-bridging across small OSM node-continuity gaps; ~20.3 miles, matching the ~21-mile figure commonly cited for the original line.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact date passenger service on this branch ended; 1958 used as an approximate placeholder matching the general national decline of branch-line passenger service in the late 1950s (see similar caveats on other short lines in this dataset), not independently confirmed for this specific line.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.speed_source: estimated typical narrow-gauge-era branch-line speed; unsourced

segments.note: Chartered in 1873 by local Santa Cruz interests (including F.A. Hihn) to end the town's rail isolation, the narrow-gauge Santa Cruz Railroad was completed in May 1876, connecting Santa Cruz via Capitola and Aptos to Pajaro, where it met the Southern Pacific's Coast Line -- Santa Cruz's first rail link to the outside world. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
